transcript.text: The sides of our new fridge freezer get really warm, almost hot, especially near the front edge. Is that a fire risk? It's in an alcove between two units.

No, it is not a fire risk. On most modern fridge-freezers, the condenser coils are built into the sides of the cabinet. However, because yours is in an alcove, we need to make sure there is enough air circulation. If the gap between the fridge sides and your cabinets is too tight (less than 2–3cm), heat can build up inside the cupboard, which might cause the appliance to work harder or trip a safety cut-out. Could you check if there is at least a finger's width of space on both sides? If it feels very hot but there is plenty of gap, just let me know.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
It's about 1cm each side, so not quite a finger's width. There's a cupboard above with a few cm gap. No burning smell or anything like that, and nothing has tripped.

1cm is most likely tighter than the recommended 2–3cm, so it is very likely that heat is getting trapped in the alcove and making the sides feel hot. This isn't a fire risk right now since there's no burning smell or tripping, but it will make the fridge work harder and use more electricity. To confirm exactly how much space your specific model needs, could you please tell me the brand and model number? It’s usually on a sticker inside the fridge, often near the salad drawer or on the side wall. If you can't reach it right now, that's fine—we can look at moving it slightly to give it more breathing room.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
It's a Hotpoint, model H7X 93T SK. I'd rather not move it though, we've just had the new floor put in and I don't want to scratch it.

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. Since you prefer not to move the appliance, we need to manage the heat build-up without shifting it. The 1cm gap is likely causing the sides to feel hot because the condenser coils (which are built into the side panels) cannot dissipate heat effectively. To fix this without moving the fridge, try placing a small, flat spacer or a couple of coins under the front corners of the feet on both sides to tilt it slightly back; this can sometimes create enough airflow gap at the bottom and top edges. Alternatively, ensure there are no items stored in that alcove above or beside it that might block air circulation. If you do this and the sides remain dangerously hot (too hot to touch comfortably for more than a few seconds) after 24 hours of running, then we may need to consider if the unit is defective, but usually, improving the airflow resolves the heat issue.
